passages.text:
Mail Call Confusion --- It’s mail call. You can’t tell if staff are hollering for you, and you have no envelopes.
[[Ask a CO after mail call, mouthing Did I get mail? Need envelope.]]
[[Give up, sit alone, feeling isolated.]]

passages.name: Untitled Passage

passages.text:
SHADOW: Shrugged off: CO- “You’ll get it if your name’s called.”

LIL WINDOW: That evening, the prison librarian passes through on rec time and—after a quiet gesture from you—slips you an envelope from her cart, no questions asked.
passages.name: Ask a CO after mail call, mouthing Did I get mail? Need envelope.

passages.text:
SHADOW Only: An ache of loneliness sets in.

LIL WINDOW: Later, a passing counselor notices and leaves you a pamphlet on “resources for new arrivals.” Inside: instructions for requesting family phone calls.

[[ Try to keep calm, show your notepad, and quietly sign “help.”]]

[[Withdraw, avoid interactions.]]

passages.text:
SHADOW: Someone mocks your gestures or tries to take advantage because you can’t hear. 

LIL WINDOW: A ''peer'' who’s seen you before steps in to de-escalate: “He’s deaf, man. Chill.” For the first time, someone has your back.
passages.name: Try to keep calm, show your intake paper, and quietly sign “help.”

passages.text:
SHADOW: Isolation builds, stress meter rises. 

LIL WINDOW: Over time, your patience pays off, the peer support group meets, and while it’s awkward, you’re able to both sign and write. This time, people listen.
passages.name: Withdraw, avoid interactions.
Try to keep calm, show your notepad, and quietly sign “help.”
